name: Giocattolo
overview: Giocattolo Motori Pty Ltd was established in 1986 in Caloundra, Queensland by automotive entrepreneur Paul Halstead and former McLaren Formula 1 engineer Barry Lock. Conceived as Australia's answer to the Ferrari 288 GTO and Porsche 959, the Giocattolo ('toy' in Italian) began with brand-new Alfa Romeo Sprint bodyshells imported from Italy. The front drivetrain was discarded, replaced by a mid-mounted Walkinshaw-fettled Holden Special Vehicles 5.0-litre Group A V8 (220kW/300hp) linked to a bespoke ZF 5-speed transaxle, Kevlar/carbon-fibre composite bodywork, and Brembo racing brakes. Capable of 0-100 km/h in 4.5 seconds and 260 km/h, the Giocattolo was an extraordinary Australian supercar feat. Only 15 production cars were completed before operations ceased in 1989.
australian_history:
Paul Halstead, a wealthy computer entrepreneur who ran 'The Toy Shop' exotic car dealership in Sydney, dreamed of creating a bespoke mid-engine Australian sports car. Partnering with Barry Lock, formerly chief engineer at McLaren F1 and Can-Am racing, they established a factory at Caloundra on the Sunshine Coast of Queensland.

Halstead initially intended to use the Alfa Romeo 2.5-litre Busso V6 mounted amidships behind the front seats. However, importing and tuning the Italian engines proved complex, expensive, and fragile. Halstead approached Tom Walkinshaw of Holden Special Vehicles (HSV). An agreement was reached for HSV to supply brand-new Holden 5.0-litre (5000i) fuel-injected V8s built to VL SS Group A Walkinshaw specifications. Halstead paired the thumping Australian V8 with an imported ZF 5DS-25/2 five-speed transaxle—the same gearbox used in the Ford GT40, De Tomaso Pantera, and BMW M1.

Lock redesigned the chassis from the bulkhead back, fabricating a rigid tubular rear spaceframe with double-wishbone independent suspension, cockpit-adjustable anti-roll bars, and four-piston Brembo disc brakes. Widebody Kevlar and carbon-fibre wheel arches gave the car an aggressive Group B rally stance. With 220 kW (300 bhp) pushing just 1,085 kg, the Giocattolo blasted from 0-100 km/h in 4.5 seconds and completed the standing quarter-mile in 12.8 seconds, comfortably out-accelerating contemporary Ferraris. However, escalating costs and the sudden withdrawal of promised Queensland State Government industrial development subsidies forced the company into liquidation in 1989. In total, only 3 Alfa V6 prototypes and 15 Holden V8 production cars were built.
